# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-29

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — "catch the reasoning errors your LLM states with
total confidence" plus the 47+28=76 example tells me what this does in five
seconds, and `pip install carnot-ebm` is right there. But trust cracks fast: a

benchmarks I've never heard of (FoVer, VeriCoT, CCTU, PREM). I'd keep reading,
but I'd start doubting the rigor — which is fatal for a project whose pitch IS
rigor.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradiction — hero badge says "MIT-0 · Open Source", footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License". The one fact an adopter checks first, and the page
   can't keep it straight.
2. Fabrication-signal cluster in Results — "0.5 → 1.0" (twice), "60/60 attacks",
   "99.3% flagged", "0.90 AUC vs 0.125 baseline" (a 7× lift over a below-chance
   baseline), all with no sample size or confidence interval on the card. Too
   perfect; undercuts the "every number backed by an artifact" promise.
3. Jargon wall + misplaced status card — FoVer / VeriCoT / CCTU / PREM /
   HalluGuard / CRANE / EstimationVerifier appear unexplained across the stats,

   card ("5-seed dual-condition; architecture-only 0.8947. Repinned from v2

   layout.

- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — perfect 1.0, meter pinned at 100%.
